basis: Amendment No. 2 to the S-1, filed Nov 10, 2026
what: Maker of the Claude AI models.

offer.dates_from: Company announcement, as reported by Yahoo Finance

side_sale: Separately, seven suppliers and partners agreed to buy $26.0B of non-voting shares at the IPO price. Those shares have no lock-up.
proceeds: General corporate purposes, including compute and infrastructure, operations and hiring. About $3.8B is set aside for tax bills on employee stock awards.

facts.label: cash and short-term investments on Sep 30, 2026
cash produced by operations, Jan to Sep 2026
committed to compute and infrastructure through 2045

financials.note: The net loss for Jan to Sep 2026 was far larger, $104.0B. Of that, $94.3B is a non-cash accounting charge for the rising value of convertible notes.

holders_note: The filing's ownership table covers voting shares only. Amazon and Google hold non-voting shares, so they are not in it. Press summaries of the filing put them at about 1.92B and 1.79B shares after the IPO, more than any co-founder.
control_note: The seven co-founders also vote one special share that carries 50.1% of all votes, and a trust elects most of the board.
rounds_note: Prices are adjusted for the 10-for-1 share split in September 2026. The filing dates only the rounds of the last three years.

lockup.summary: Insider shares are released in stages over 365 days, not on a single date.

events.what: Up to 10% of what employees and non-founder insiders hold
One release, then five more two weeks apart
End of the 180-day lock-up; co-founders may sell up to 29% of theirs
Releases tied to first- and second-quarter results
End of the 365-day lock-up for co-founders and large holders

risks: Its AI models have behaved, and may behave, in unintended ways, including taking harmful actions no user directed.
Its success depends on building the most capable AI models.
It may fail to secure enough computing power to train models and serve customers.
If its computing needs differ from its forecasts, it may have too little or be committed to too much.
Shortages of chips, memory, power or data-centre capacity could limit its access to computing power.
risks_note: The first five risk factors, summarised.
